questions.question: Email outages keep returning even though the service desk restores service for users each time. An IT manager opens a problem record. What is Problem Management's goal in this situation?

options.text: Restore normal service for each affected user quickly
Identify and resolve the underlying cause of outages
Control the life cycle of the changes needed for a fix
Fulfill the catalog requests that affected users submit

explanation.correct: ServiceNow describes Problem Management as having a single goal: identifying and resolving the underlying issues that cause incidents. It is a methodical process in which finding and resolving the root cause matters more than time to resolution, which is exactly what recurring email outages call for once service has been restored each time. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/understanding-state-mgmt-transitions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Restoring normal service while minimizing impact is the purpose of Incident Management, which the service desk is already doing for each outage.
Controlling the life cycle of changes is Change Management. A change request may later be raised to apply the fix, but that is not the problem's goal.
Submitting and fulfilling requests for services and products through a self-service portal is Request Management, not Problem Management.

source.excerpt: Problem Management refers to the process of identifying and resolving the underlying cause of one or more incidents.

questions.question: A problem manager wants the root cause and workaround of a known problem to be searchable so agents can deflect new incidents. They click Create Known Error Article on the problem. Where is the article kept?

options.text: As a work note on each incident related to the problem
In a knowledge base maintained in Knowledge Management
As an attribute on the affected CI record in the CMDB
In a change request raised from the problem record

explanation.correct: Known error articles document the root cause and workaround of a problem to help deflect incidents. When an article is created from a problem, it is saved in the knowledge base and maintained in the Knowledge Management application, where the knowledge base's workflows control publishing and retirement. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/create-known-error-from-problem.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Copying text into the work notes of related incidents is what Communicate Workaround does; it notifies existing incidents but does not create a searchable article.
The CMDB associates the problem with affected configuration items, but known error content is not stored on the CI; the article lives in a knowledge base.
A change request from a problem is used to implement the fix to the root cause. It does not store the known error documentation for agents to search.

source.excerpt: The known error database is a repository of problem records that a company has designated as known issues.

questions.question: What is the difference between reactive and proactive problem detection?

options.text: Reactive requires approval; proactive does not
Reactive is triggered by incidents; proactive identifies problems through trend analysis before incidents occur
Reactive is automated; proactive is manual
There is no difference between them

explanation.correct: If a problem is detected reactively, one or more incidents have already taken place, prompting an investigation. Proactive problem detection identifies problems through trend analysis or other means before incidents occur. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=f782895d93d09a5c56aeb94c5cba1044&child_id=0ea249d947dc9a5089c7acc9126d4364&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Approval requirements don't define reactive vs proactive detection.
Both reactive and proactive can be automated or manual.
There is a clear difference in timing - reactive is after incidents, proactive is before.

source.excerpt: If a problem is detected reactively, it means that one or more incidents have already taken place, prompting an investigation to uncover the root cause of the issue.

questions.question: Which role is required to reopen a problem record in ServiceNow?

options.text: problem_admin
problem_task_analyst
problem_manager
itil

explanation.correct: The problem_manager role is required to reopen a problem record. This user can create and update problems, problem tasks, and related records, administer problem properties, and is the only role that can reopen a problem record. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=f782895d93d09a5c56aeb94c5cba1044&child_id=0ea249d947dc9a5089c7acc9126d4364&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: problem_admin can create, update, and delete problems but cannot reopen them.
problem_task_analyst can only create and update problem tasks, not reopen problems.
The itil role is a general ITSM role and doesn't specifically grant problem reopen capability.

source.excerpt: This user can also administer problem properties, and this is the only role that could reopen a problem record. So someone serving as a manager would need this role.

questions.question: What are the three main stages of the problem lifecycle?

options.text: Create, Assign, Close
Detection and Logging, Investigation and Diagnosis, Resolution and Closure
New, In Progress, Resolved
Submit, Review, Approve

explanation.correct: The lifecycle for managing problems starts with detecting and logging them, then moving into investigation and diagnosis, and finally concluding with resolution and closure. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=f782895d93d09a5c56aeb94c5cba1044&child_id=0ea249d947dc9a5089c7acc9126d4364&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: These are actions, not the formal problem lifecycle stages.
These are incident states, not the problem lifecycle stages.
These relate more to approval processes, not problem lifecycle.

source.excerpt: The life cycle for managing problems starts with detecting and logging them, then moving into investigation and diagnosis, and finally concluding with resolution and closure.

questions.question: No permanent fix exists yet for a problem, but the team has found a way for users to keep working. The coordinator fills in the Workaround field and clicks Communicate Workaround. What is the purpose of the workaround?

options.text: To record the permanent fix that removes the root cause
To lessen the impact until an actual resolution exists
To resolve and close every related incident in one step
To publish a known error article to the knowledge base

explanation.correct: ServiceNow defines a workaround as a temporary way to restore service failures and lessen the impact of a problem for which an actual resolution is not yet available. Communicating it notifies the related incidents that a workaround is available, so agents and users can keep working while root cause analysis and the permanent fix continue. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/communicate-workaround.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: A workaround is temporary by definition. The permanent fix is documented separately and is usually applied through a change request before the problem is resolved.
Communicate Workaround copies the workaround to the related incidents' work notes and comments and sends notifications; it does not change their state to Resolved.
Known error articles are created with the separate Create Known Error Article related link. The legacy docs note that communicating a workaround does not create a knowledge article.

source.excerpt: Our goal in Problem Management is to identify the root cause of incidents, find feasible workarounds, and implement permanent solutions that prevent future occurrences.

questions.question: Multiple users report the same network connectivity issue. What should the service desk do?

options.text: Create separate incidents and wait for them to resolve themselves
Create incidents and a problem record to investigate the root cause
Ignore the reports until a manager intervenes
Submit a change request immediately

explanation.correct: A problem can arise when the same or similar incidents occur repeatedly. Creating a problem record allows investigation of the root cause while incidents handle the immediate user impact. The problem investigation aims to prevent future occurrences. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=f782895d93d09a5c56aeb94c5cba1044&child_id=0ea249d947dc9a5089c7acc9126d4364&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Recurring incidents indicate a potential underlying problem that should be investigated.
Service desk should actively manage and escalate recurring issues.
A change request should follow after the root cause is identified, not before.

source.excerpt: A problem can also arise when the same or similar incidents occur repeatedly, without a clear understanding of the root cause.

questions.question: What tabs are available on the Problem form for documenting investigation details? (Choose two)

options.text: Analysis Information
Service Level Agreements
Resolution Information
Approval History

explanation.correct: The form has tabs including Analysis Information (for root cause and workarounds), Resolution Information (for permanent fix details), and Other Information (for reporter details). The Notes tab is also available for work notes. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=f782895d93d09a5c56aeb94c5cba1044&child_id=0ea249d947dc9a5089c7acc9126d4364&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: SLA tracking is more relevant to incidents than problems.
Approval History is used in Change Management, not Problem forms.

source.excerpt: The form has three tabs, Analysis Information, Resolution Information, and Other Information.

questions.question: How does the CMDB support problem management processes?

options.text: By automatically resolving problems when CIs are updated
By providing insights for troubleshooting through CI relationships and dependencies
By creating problem records whenever a CI is added
By generating root cause analysis reports automatically

explanation.correct: The CMDB stores information about all components of an information system. Every service management process involves the CMDB. If there's an issue and you need to find the root cause, the CMDB provides valuable insights for troubleshooting through CI relationships.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The CMDB provides information for troubleshooting but doesn't automatically resolve problems.
Adding a CI doesn't automatically create problem records.
Root cause analysis requires human investigation; the CMDB provides data to support it.

questions.question: An administrator needs a map of how the applications and hosts behind an online ordering service connect, so the impact of a failing component is visible. Which approach does Service Mapping use?

options.text: Horizontal discovery that lists each device independently
Top-down mapping of connections between devices and apps
Manual entry of each CI relationship by an administrator
Correlating third-party monitoring alerts with known CIs

explanation.correct: Service Mapping maps dependencies based on the connections between devices and applications, which ServiceNow calls top-down mapping. The resulting application service maps show infrastructure objects and the connections between them, so a faulty object appears together with the devices and applications it affects. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-operations-management/itom-visibility/itom-visibility-landing-page.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Horizontal discovery is what Discovery performs. It finds devices and applications but connections between them are not included, so it cannot show service impact.
Service Mapping builds maps automatically, mainly with discovery patterns, and can also use tags and traffic connections; it does not rely on manual relationship entry.
Correlating alerts from third-party monitoring tools with configuration items is ITOM AIOps, which consumes ITOM Visibility data rather than building service maps.

questions.question: A database server failure causes an HR requisition system to stop working. Which CMDB feature would best help identify all affected services?

options.text: CI Class Manager
Schema Map
Dependency View map
Tables and Columns module

explanation.correct: The Dependency View map shows upstream and downstream dependencies between configuration items. It would show that losing the database server affects the application, which in turn disrupts services like the HR requisition system.

wrongAnswers.explanation: CI Class Manager shows the class hierarchy and metadata, not runtime dependencies.
Schema Map shows table relationships in the database, not CI dependencies.
Tables and Columns module shows database structure, not service dependencies.

questions.question: Discovery has populated the CMDB with servers and applications, but an administrator still cannot see which of them depend on each other to deliver the payroll service. What explains this?

options.text: Discovery stores connections, but they are hidden by default
Discovery omits connections; Service Mapping maps them
Discovery finds network devices only, not the applications
Service Mapping replaces Discovery and ignores its CI results

explanation.correct: Discovery performs horizontal discovery: it identifies computers, servers, network devices and the applications running on them, but connections between devices and applications are not included. Service Mapping fills that gap with top-down mapping that maps dependencies based on those connections, and it builds on the results of horizontal discovery. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-operations-management/itom-visibility/itom-visibility-landing-page.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The docs state that connections between devices and applications are not included in horizontal discovery, so there is nothing hidden to reveal.
Discovery can find IP-enabled devices and the applications that run on them, as well as cloud resources and TLS certificates, not just network gear.
Service Mapping relies on Discovery and the MID Server and uses the results of horizontal discovery performed by Discovery, rather than replacing it.

questions.question: What is the difference between a 'Known Error' and a 'Problem' in ServiceNow?

options.text: A Known Error is a Problem where the root cause has been identified and a workaround documented
Known Errors are more severe than Problems
Problems track incidents; Known Errors track change requests
There is no difference; they are the same record type

explanation.correct: A Problem becomes a Known Error when root cause analysis is complete and either a workaround or permanent fix has been identified. Known Errors are documented so that if the issue recurs, the service desk can apply the workaround immediately.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Severity is not the distinction; Known Errors represent investigated Problems with identified root causes.
Both Problems and Known Errors exist on the Problem table; they don't track different record types.
Known Error is a specific state/phase of a Problem record, indicating root cause has been identified.

questions.question: An administrator notices that 15 incidents over the past month all relate to the same printer failing. What is the FIRST step in the Problem Management process?

options.text: Create a Problem record and associate the related incidents
Close all 15 incidents as duplicates
Order a replacement printer immediately
Create a Change Request to replace the printer

explanation.correct: The first step is creating a Problem record and linking the related incidents. This begins formal root cause analysis and provides a single tracking point for the recurring issue. Solutions (change requests, replacements) come after root cause analysis.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Closing incidents as duplicates loses individual tracking and doesn't address the underlying problem.
Ordering a replacement before root cause analysis may not solve the actual problem (could be a network or driver issue, not hardware).
A Change Request may eventually be needed, but root cause analysis through the Problem must come first.

questions.question: Which activity is part of 'proactive' Problem Management?

options.text: Analyzing incident trends to identify potential problems before they cause major outages
Creating Problem records only after a Major Incident occurs
Closing all open Problems at the end of each quarter
Assigning every incident to the Problem Management team

explanation.correct: Proactive Problem Management involves analyzing trends, reviewing recurring incidents, and identifying patterns that indicate underlying problems — before they escalate into major outages. This is preventive rather than reactive.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Creating Problems only after Major Incidents is reactive, not proactive.
Closing Problems on a schedule without resolution is poor practice and not proactive management.
Not every incident needs Problem Management involvement; proactive analysis focuses on patterns and trends.

questions.question: A service desk agent has an incident On Hold with the reason Awaiting Problem. Its linked problem is then resolved with the resolution code Fix Applied, using the Madrid problem state model. What happens to the incident?

options.text: It stays On Hold until an agent resolves it manually
It moves to In Progress so the assignee can verify the fix
It is set to Resolved with the code Resolved by problem
It receives the fix in work notes but stays On Hold

explanation.correct: With the Problem Management Best Practice - Madrid - State Model plugin, an incident that is On Hold with the reason Awaiting Problem is updated automatically when its problem is resolved or closed with Fix Applied. The incident state changes to Resolved, its resolution code becomes Resolved by problem, and the caller and assignee are emailed. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/it-service-management/problem-management/sync-btwn-inci-prob.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Manual resolution is not needed here. For incidents awaiting a problem, resolving the problem with Fix Applied sets the incident to Resolved automatically.
The documented outcome for an On Hold, Awaiting Problem incident is the Resolved state, not In Progress, when the problem is resolved with Fix Applied.
Copying the fix to work notes without changing state describes the Communicate Fix related link. Resolving the problem with Fix Applied also resolves the waiting incident.
